default.en: Cycle data not supplied — biological window not scored.
default.hi: चक्र सम्बन्धी जानकारी नहीं — जैविक अवसर अगणित।

meta.note: Phases are produced by cycleModel() from LMP, cycle length and bleeding days; the luteal constant and the width of the fertile window are profile data, not literals in code. Ritukala — the classical prescription that the samskara belongs to the sixteen nights following the cessation of menses — coincides closely with the modern fertile window, and both are represented here.
meta.omitted_deliberately: Muhurta Chintamani and the Smritis contain rules assigning even nights to male offspring and odd nights to female offspring. These rules are NOT implemented, scored or displayed anywhere in this module. Sex selection is prohibited in India under the PCPNDT Act, 1994, and rendering such a rule as actionable guidance would be both unlawful and against the purpose of this tool.
meta.disclaimer: This is a calendar-method estimate, not medical advice. Ovulation prediction kits, follicular monitoring and a qualified physician are more accurate.

translations.en: Menstruation — union is prohibited for the whole of the rajasvala period.
translations.hi: रजस्वला काल — इस अवधि में सहवास पूर्णत: वर्जित।

rules.interpretation: The prohibition is unanimous across the Smritis and the Muhurta texts, and coincides with the period in which conception is not possible. This is the strongest single bar in the module.

translations.en: The first four nights from the onset of menses are excluded from the Ritukala.
translations.hi: रजोदर्शन से प्रथम चार रात्रि ऋतुकाल से बहिष्कृत।

rules.interpretation: The classical Ritukala is counted as the sixteen nights beginning from the onset of menses, of which the first four are expressly excluded. Where bleeding lasts longer than four days the menses rule governs instead.

translations.en: Early follicular phase — within the Ritukala but conception is unlikely.
translations.hi: पूर्व-कूपिक अवस्था — ऋतुकाल में, किन्तु गर्भधारण की सम्भावना अल्प।

rules.interpretation: Permitted by the shastra and not prohibited, but several days before the fertile window opens.

translations.en: Fertile window opening — conception is possible.
translations.hi: उर्वर काल का आरम्भ — गर्भधारण सम्भव।

rules.interpretation: Roughly five to four days before the estimated ovulation. Sperm survival makes conception possible from here onward.

exceptions.note: Irregular cycle — the window position is uncertain, so the estimate is discounted.

translations.en: Highly fertile — the two to three days before ovulation.
translations.hi: अत्यन्त उर्वर — अण्डोत्सर्ग से दो-तीन दिन पूर्व।

rules.interpretation: The days immediately preceding ovulation carry the highest observed conception rates.

exceptions.note: Irregular cycle — the estimate is discounted and an ovulation kit is advised.

translations.en: Peak fertility — the estimated day of ovulation and the day either side.
translations.hi: चरम उर्वरता — अनुमानित अण्डोत्सर्ग एवं उसके आगे-पीछे का दिन।

rules.interpretation: The biological optimum. This is the component the whole module is ordered around: a scripturally perfect day outside the fertile window cannot produce a conception, so biology is weighted first.

exceptions.note: Irregular cycle — ovulation day cannot be reliably placed by the calendar method.

translations.en: Just past ovulation — the window is closing.
translations.hi: अण्डोत्सर्ग के तुरन्त पश्चात् — अवसर घट रहा है।

rules.interpretation: The ovum remains viable for roughly a day after release; conception is possible but the probability falls sharply.

translations.en: Luteal phase — conception from this cycle is no longer possible.
translations.hi: ल्यूटियल अवस्था — इस चक्र में गर्भधारण अब सम्भव नहीं।

rules.interpretation: Not prohibited by the shastra, but outside the purpose of a Garbhadhana muhurta. The next cycle's window is projected instead.

translations.en: Beyond the sixteen nights of the Ritukala.
translations.hi: ऋतुकाल की सोलह रात्रियों के पश्चात्।

rules.interpretation: The classical Ritukala closes on the sixteenth night from the onset of menses. Deliberately modelled as a PENALTY rather than as a biological phase: in a long cycle the estimated ovulation can fall on or after the seventeenth night, and the shastric and the biological readings then genuinely disagree. Scoring them as separate terms lets the report show both instead of silently suppressing one.
